dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: "Fresh breeze in the night" or "Fresh night breeze"? How about just "Night breeze"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: I'm pulling my hair out on how to win her heart.

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: "Fresh breeze in the night" has too much emphasis on time, when I think about her day and night.

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: On the other hand, "Fresh night breeze" sounds rather cliche, like a line in a child's fairytale.

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: But just "Night breeze" would save more room for more serenade.

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: But the people in the square discussing the candidates for the next Grand Conservator are messing up my thoughts. If only I could have a quieter place to think.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry to disturb...

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: "Night breeze"... "Be my words"...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How about indoors?

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: Tried it, didn't work.

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: You got either couples flirting, or someone pushing fliers on choir, card games, cross country, and other events on you in the study.

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: I could have just stayed in the dorm room, but my dumb roommate tried to make hotpot with a prototype burner...

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: I won't go into details, except the room is still full of smoke.

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: I don't trust myself to write anything Hana will appreciate in that condition.

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: Ahem... "Melodious night breeze, be my words, express the daylight delights"...

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: "Here I stand in the wind, just to hear your gentle sing-along."

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: What do you think of that?

dialogues.speaker: Hana
dialogues.text: What do I think of what?

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: The lovely poem I just composed. How does it make you feel?

dialogues.speaker: Hana
dialogues.text: Is this... for your literature class?

dialogues.speaker: Hana
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I don't quite get it...

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: That's okay, just listen closely...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The next Grand Conservator?

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: Yes, the current Grand Conservator announced a few days ago that he was going to retire, and the next Grand Conservator needs to be voted in by the sages.

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: Practically everyone is talking about this. Didn't you hear them chattering about it?

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: Something about Vikram of the Vahumana being good with people, and Rifaet of the Haravatat being incredibly intellectual. Stuff like that...

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: I think there're even fan clubs of some sorts that've been set up by some students. From what I see, there's too little schoolwork.

dialogues.speaker: Ziryab
dialogues.text: Hana's better. She doesn't care about these mundane things.
